Øvemål · Niveau 2 Lyt til basslag, rim-klik og shaker som forskellige rytmiske lag. Her spiller rim-stemmen et helt 3–2-mønster: tre slag i første takt og to i anden. Vi skriver forløbet som to hele takter i 4/4 med ottendedele som underdeling. Det samme rytmiske forhold kan noteres i to takter 2/4 med sekstendedele; tempoet skal tilpasses, hvis varigheden skal være den samme. Figuren er et almindeligt bossa nova-grundmønster, ikke en fast regel for al bossa eller en afro-cubansk son-clave. !! Prøv selv * Lyt først, og klap kun den øverste stemme. * Tæl to takter som én sammenhængende rytmisk frase. * Klap de tre rim-slag i første takt og de to i anden. Bevar underdelingen gennem pauserne. * Lav en kopi af nodearket og ændr én rytme uden at miste pulsen. !! Min øvelseslog Skriv her, hvad du opdager, og hvordan du ændrer rytmen i din egen kopi. ","huwiki-text-en":"! Learning goal · Level 2 Listen to bass drum, rim click and shaker as distinct rhythmic layers. The rim voice plays a complete 3–2 figure: three hits in the first bar and two in the second. We write it as two complete bars of 4/4 with eighth-note subdivisions. The same rhythmic proportions can be written as two bars of 2/4 with sixteenth notes; adjust the tempo if the duration is to stay the same. This figure is a common bossa nova pattern, not a fixed rule for all bossa nova or an Afro-Cuban son clave. !! Try it * First listen and clap only the upper voice. * Count two bars as one continuous rhythmic phrase. * Clap the three rim hits in the first bar and the two in the second. Keep the subdivisions going through the rests. * Copy the score and change one rhythm without losing the pulse. !! My practice log Write what you notice and how you change the rhythm in your own copy. Lyt til formkontrasten En original 16-takters AABA-melodi: A-stykker i afdæmpet ''bossa nova'', B-stykket i mere aktiv ''samba'', og sidste A tilbage til bossa. Prøv at skifte stil til ren bossa eller samba og sammenlign. Hør især tamborim, shaker, baspuls og synkoper. ! Min kompositionsidé Lav din egen B-del, eller ændr akkordforløbet i en kopi. ","huwiki-text-en":"! Listen for contrast between sections An original 16-bar AABA tune: quiet ''bossa nova'' A sections, a livelier ''samba'' B section, and a final return to bossa. Try selecting pure bossa or samba and compare. Listen especially to tamborim, shaker, bass pulse and syncopations. ! My composition idea Compose your own B section or change the chord progression in a copy. HUWIKI · MUSIC LAB

Rhythms to hear,
see and transform.

Start with a two-bar pattern, listen and make your own version. These open ABC exercises can be copied, edited and used in your own compositions.

Balkan 7/8 · melodies and chords

Three patterns—3+2+2, 2+2+3 and 2+3+2—with original melodies, chord symbols and percussion. [[Open the 7/8 workshop|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Balkan]]

India · Konnakol and tāla

Syllable rhythms, subdivisions, clapped cycles and original melodies to explore.

[[Open the Konnakol lessons|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Indien]]

Afro-Cuban clave rhythms

The two bars belong together: three hits followed by two or the other way around. Rumba clave shifts one of the accents.

[[Son clave 3–2|Rytmik – Son-clave 3–2]] · [[Son clave 2–3|Rytmik – Son-clave 2–3]] · [[Rumba clave 3–2|Rytmik – Rumba-clave 3–2]]

Brazilian rhythms

Follow the surdo bass pulse, rim/tamborim and shaker. Listen to laid-back bossa nova and lively samba. They are related but should not be confused with son clave.

[[Bossa · 2 bars|Rytmik – Bossa nova 2 takter]] · [[Samba · 2 bars|Rytmik – Samba 2 takter]]

Balkan · asymmetric meters

Read and play short 7/8, 9/8 and 11/8 patterns with different beat groupings.

[[Open Balkan rhythms|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Balkan]]

From rhythm to composition

[[Rio study: A=bossa and B=samba|Rio-studie – A bossa, B samba]] is an original tune showing how bossa and samba can alternate between A and B sections.

Suggested teaching sequence

  1. Listen without playing—what instruments do you hear?
  2. Clap and count over two bars.
  3. Explore notes and syncopations.
  4. Copy the example, write your own variation and keep a short practice log.
  5. Combine your rhythm with a melody and publish your work via HUWiki Site.
